correctness.rationale: The equilibrium conditions are necessary and sufficient: no buyer can be nominated, every nonbuyer must be nominated, each buyer nominates k distinct vertices, and all q nonbuyers must be covered. Inclusion-exclusion gives the exact count. The asymptotic proof uses an explicit lower bound at q=floor(n/log n), a uniform upper envelope g_n(q), strict concavity, and an exponential gap outside every fixed relative neighborhood of n/log n. The cost-ratio corollaries follow from Q_n/n→0 in probability.

originality.rationale: The nearest primary paper proves the price-of-anarchy bound and identifies an extremal equilibrium, but does not count all labelled equilibrium profiles or establish their uniform-profile asymptotic distribution. Inspected earlier public-goods models use different strategy spaces. Targeted literature-index searches found no directly equivalent record; this supports but does not prove novelty.
residual_risks: Semantic literature-index retrieval and the inspected literature cannot prove absence of all unpublished, unindexed, or differently phrased prior work.
Uniform sampling over labelled pure-equilibrium profiles is a mathematical reference measure, not a claim about empirically realistic equilibrium selection.
The asymptotic theorem requires fixed k; the proof does not cover k growing with n or non-complete digraphs.

value.rationale: The result quantifies equilibrium multiplicity in the canonical complete-digraph benchmark and shows that, under uniform profile counting, almost all pure equilibria have near-maximal buyer count and asymptotically worst-case cost. This adds a distinct equilibrium-selection baseline beyond existence and price-of-anarchy extrema.
